The generated model omits both gateways, so the activities are not synchronized as the description requires. This is the pattern LRN-022 already covers, so the guideline is a reinforcement of an existing learned rule rather th)

refines EVT-01 (The generated model uses a start event "Customer reports issue" for an occurrence that the description places after delivery, inside the process. The reference instead has a task after the "International order?" gateway. EVT-01 covers start events only for process triggers, so it does not say how to handle a mid-process occurrence. This guideline adds that case. The records do not fully establish )

same as LRN-022 (The reference has a parallel split after the completed step and a parallel join before the later step, and the generated model has neither gateway. The description (S12) says the order is dispatched once packaging and shipping documents are ready, and the inventory update and shipping confirmation then follow without any stated order. Both the split and the join are required, since the later step )

refines FID-02 (The reference splits the outcome into separate tasks after an exclusive gateway (M6, with a separate task for the replacement case in M3), while the generated model merged the alternatives into one task labelled 'Process refund or replacement' (P4, S19). FID-02 already says not to merge separately described actions, but it does not say how to handle alternatives joined by 'or'. This guideline adds)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the company itself receives or confirms an outcome of a step, and a next action follows directly after it, with no stated waiting time and no external message or condition the process waits for: Model that outcome as a task performed by the company, placed in the sequence before the next action. Use an intermediate catch event or an event-based gateway only when the description states that the process waits for an external message, signal, time or condition.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the company itself receives or confirms an outcome of a step, and a next action follows directly after it, with no stated waiting time and no external message or condition the process waits for

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that an activity follows the receipt of an item or delivery (for example 'upon receiving X, ...'), and it does not describe any message, signal, time or condition that the process waits for: Do not insert an intermediate catch event for the receipt. Connect the preceding activity directly by a sequence flow to the first activity the description gives after the receipt. Use an intermediate catch event only when the description states a wait for an external message, signal, timer or condition.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description states a step that a participant performs or that the process completes, given as a verb phrase (for example reporting, placing, receiving or processing something), and it places a later step directly after that step, while naming no message, signal, timer or condition that the process waits for.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several actions that all occur after one completed step, with no condition choosing among them, and a later step is reached only after all of those actions are finished: Model a parallel gateway split directly after the completed step, with one outgoing sequence flow to each listed action, and a matching parallel gateway join that collects those actions before the later step. Do not use an exclusive gateway or a condition on these branches.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description lists two or more activities that all follow one completed step, with no condition or order among them, and a later step is reached only after all of those activities are finished (for example, 'once X and Y are ready' or 'meanwhile' work that must finish before the next step)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a customer report or external occurrence that happens partway through the process, after an earlier step such as delivery, rather than as the event that starts the process: Do not model such an occurrence as a start event. Start events are only for triggers that begin the process. Model the mid-process occurrence as an intermediate catch event at the point where it happens, and keep the step that follows it as a separate activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a customer report or external occurrence that happens partway through the process, after an earlier step such as delivery, rather than as the event that starts the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names alternative outcomes of one activity, joined by 'or', where only one of the alternatives will be carried out: Model each named alternative as its own task placed after an exclusive gateway that splits the flow, and do not merge the alternatives into one task whose label lists them all.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names alternative outcomes of one activity, joined by 'or', where only one of the alternatives will be carried out
